substrate: GEO GSE144621 peak tiles, leave_peak_out, ceiling 0.941

preregistered.question: does rank-averaging the learned conv encoder with the biophysical max_tx scalar beat the scalar alone on the tile rung?

precondition.name: orthogonality
precondition.rule: a naive rank-average lifts only when the modalities are ORTHOGONAL; a near-chance second modality REDUCES the signal (measured: ESM2+ProSST 0.204 vs ESM2 0.352 on CTX-M-14, because ProSST alone was at chance)
precondition.not_a_gate: the orthogonality number is REPORTED, not used to skip the run -- a prediction that a combine will fail is not a substitute for measuring it

preregistered.control: max_tx rank-averaged with a SHUFFLED conv vector; if this lifts, the gain is an artifact of rank-averaging rather than of the conv's content

verdicts.HYBRID_ADDS: paired median >= +0.02 over max_tx AND >= 8/10 seeds win AND control clean
verdicts.WEAK: gain > 0 but below the margin or the seed count
verdicts.NO_GAIN: no positive paired gain -- the learned encoder carries nothing orthogonal here
verdicts.INDETERMINATE_CONTROL_ALSO_LIFTS: the shuffled-conv control lifts too; the combine, not the conv, is producing the number
verdicts.INDETERMINATE_RECONCILE_FAILED: the prediction table's published anchors drift
verdicts.INDETERMINATE_MISSING_SCORER: conv or max_tx absent from the table
verdicts.INDETERMINATE_SHORT_ARM: an arm scored fewer seeds than were loaded, so its median is taken over a different seed set than its comparator's and the two are not comparable

stacking.question: does a THIRD channel add over the MEASURED 2-channel hybrid, rather than over the scalar alone?
stacking.mirrors: the parent bar above (margin 0.02, 8 of 10 seeds), itself mirroring scripts/promcalc_decomposition_arm.py PREREGISTERED. Reused VERBATIM rather than derived, so the two 'does more information help?' results stay directly comparable; the inheritance is recorded as an inheritance, not as a derivation.
stacking.predicted_outcome: decomposition-as-third is predicted to LOSE, and to lose by MORE than gc did. Measured pairwise orthogonality (10-seed median) puts decomposition <-> max_tx at +0.7812, against gc <-> max_tx's +0.5508, so decomposition is the MORE redundant of the two available third channels -- and gc-as-third already lost (0.4217 against the 2-channel's 0.4254). The expected verdict is therefore NO_STACK for both new combos.
stacking.negative_scope: a negative closes THESE FOUR SCORERS on THIS rung, not stacking in general. conv and gc are both composition-family; max_tx and decomposition are both readings of the same Promoter Calculator output, max_tx being a scalar reduction of it. So the four span only TWO modality families, and a channel from a NEW family is untested here. A negative is evidence about the available channels, never about the mechanism.

verdicts.STACKS: paired median >= +0.02 over hybrid_conv_maxtx AND >= 8/10 seeds win
verdicts.WEAK_STACK: gain > 0 AND >= min_seeds_winning seeds win, but below the margin -- a REPRODUCIBLE gain that fell short of the effect-size bar
verdicts.INDETERMINATE_GAIN_NOT_REPRODUCIBLE: gain > 0 but FEWER than min_seeds_winning seeds win -- a positive gain that did NOT reproduce, which is neither a measured stack nor a measured negative and must not be read as either
verdicts.NO_STACK: no positive paired gain -- the third channel carries nothing the measured 2-channel hybrid lacks
verdicts.INDETERMINATE_STACKING_NOT_MEASURED: no superset combo produced a paired statistic -- a MISSING measurement, which must not be read as a negative one

honest_limits: The combine is label-free and parameter-free (a rank-average), so it RANKS and does not dose -- the same deployability class as the inverse cell.
Both inputs are out-of-sample on each seed's held-out peaks, so no second-level leakage is introduced; but the pool is MEASURED peak tiles, not generator output.
One rung, one experiment, one combine rule. A negative does not show that no learned representation can add here -- only that THIS encoder, rank-averaged with THIS scalar, does not.
`max_tx` and `conv` are both fitted by ridge on the same split, so their errors may be correlated through the split rather than through the biology.

The STACKING question puts more than one superset combo against ONE pre-registered bar and the aggregate stacking verdict is the best of them. That is a multiple-comparison exposure: with k combos the chance one clears the margin by noise exceeds the bar's nominal rate, so read the per-combo block, not only the aggregate.

Orthogonality here is Spearman between PREDICTION vectors. Two scorers can be rank-correlated and still carry complementary error structure; a rank-average is only sensitive to the rank relationship, which is why this is the measure the arm uses -- it is not a general claim that the channels share information.

SCOPE on the direction finding, and it bounds what this arm showed: `max_tx` and `decomposition` are NOT two modalities, they are two readings of ONE Promoter Calculator output -- scripts/glm_tile_predictions.py passes the same decomposition dict to both `tile_features()` and `max_tx_scalar()`, the latter being a scalar REDUCTION of it (`log1p(max Tx_rate)`). So their +0.7812 redundancy is mechanically expected, and the pair that is most redundant while still stacking is a REDUCTION/SUPERSET pair. Pairwise prediction-vector Spearman is refuted as a screen ACROSS THAT PAIR; it is NOT shown invalid between genuinely different modality families, which remain untested here. Read the result as 'finer-grained access to a channel already present pays', not as 'a new kind of information pays'.

The CI is a normal approximation on the MEAN with z=1.96, while every point estimate reported beside it is the MEDIAN -- two different estimands -- and at n=10 the correct critical value is t(9)=2.262, so these intervals are ~15% narrower than their nominal level. RE-DERIVED under t and the conclusion SURVIVES on all three combos (decomposition [0.0103, 0.0177] and gc+decomposition [0.0030, 0.0165] still exclude zero; gc still includes it), with sign tests corroborating independently (p=0.00098 / 0.0107 / 0.828). Nothing published here is wrong. It is NOT fixed because `paired()` lives in promcalc_decomposition_arm and is SHARED with the published parent arm, so correcting it moves parent numbers and needs its own pre-registration.
